saju.extraIntro: A few more traditional saju markers layered on top of your chart

shenshaContent.taohua: Peach Blossom (도화살) is often misread as a warning about romantic trouble, but it really points to a natural magnetism — the kind of presence that draws people in and keeps a room easy to talk to. You likely make a strong first impression without trying, and people tend to gravitate toward you in social settings.
shenshaContent.yima: Traveling Horse (역마살) has a reputation for restlessness, but it's really an active energy that isn't afraid of movement or change. New places and new people tend to show up often in your life, and you're the type who actually finds your luck opening up in unfamiliar environments — travel, new cities, new communities.
shenshaContent.hwagae: Canopy (화개살) is sometimes called a "lonely" marker, but it's really a sign of deep focus and artistic sensibility. You draw real energy from time alone, and your actual skill tends to show up most clearly when you're deep in something you genuinely care about.
shenshaContent.noneText: No shensha stands out sharply in your chart, which points to a steady, well-balanced temperament rather than any dramatic tilt. You're more likely to hold your pace through consistency than through sudden swings.

has.text: With a Heavenly Nobleman in your chart, you tend to have the right person or opportunity show up right when things get hard. Keeping your relationships with mentors and people above you in good shape now pays off exactly when you need it most.

none.text: No Heavenly Nobleman in this chart just means your path leans more on your own effort than outside help. You tend to trust your own judgment and push things through yourself — and whatever you build that way is fully, unambiguously yours.

same.text: {{year}} moves in step with your own energy. It's a year for familiar rhythms, so staying consistent with what you're already doing is likely to pay off.

otherGeneratesMe.subheading: A Year That Fills You Up
otherGeneratesMe.text: {{year}} tends to feed and support you. Help and opportunity show up around you with less effort than usual, so things are likely to move more smoothly than you'd expect.

iGenerateOther.text: {{year}} asks you to give more than you receive. What you put in tends to come back as real results, so it's worth pacing yourself while you pour energy into what actually matters to you.

otherOvercomesMe.text: {{year}} brings more friction than flow. Friction doesn't mean a bad year — it's more likely to be one that toughens you up — so move a little more carefully on big decisions and keep an eye on your health as you go.

iOvercomeOther.subheading: A Year You're In Charge Of
iOvercomeOther.text: {{year}} puts you in the driver's seat. Your judgment and drive are sharper than usual, making it a good year to finally start something you've been putting off.

current.text: You're currently in a Samjae period ({{start}}-{{end}}). Samjae doesn't mean the years are cursed — it really just means a stretch with more change packed into it than usual. Move a little more carefully on big decisions and pay a bit more attention to your health, and this stretch can end up being the launchpad for what comes after.

upcoming.text: Your next Samjae period is {{start}}-{{end}}. There's no rush — just worth keeping in mind for later. When it arrives, move a little more carefully on big decisions and take a bit better care of your health.

same.text:
In the Five Element cycle, {{my}} and {{other}} sit in exactly the same place — not two forces meeting, but one energy showing up twice. That's the real mechanism behind how easy this feels: there's no translation layer between you, no adjusting your register before you speak. Whatever you'd say to yourself in your own head is close enough to what they'd say too, and that kind of overlap is rare enough to actually notice.

The place to stay a little alert is exactly where the comfort comes from: two people this alike can reinforce the same blind spot instead of covering for each other's. Use the ease deliberately — bring it into the moments that need trust, and every so often, invite a genuinely different read into the room. Matching energy is a resource, not a script; the more you actually use it instead of coasting on it, the more it pays off.

otherGeneratesMe.text:
In the Five Element cycle, {{other}} generates {{my}} — their energy doesn't just sit next to yours, it actively feeds it. That's why this tends to feel less like effort and more like relief: you show up a little steadier after time with them, without either of you doing anything dramatic to make that happen. It's one of the more sustainable dynamics there is, because the support isn't a favor being called in, it's just how the two energies naturally move.

The one thing worth watching is where the support is actually coming from over time — a generating relationship works best when you're also building your own steadiness alongside it, not quietly outsourcing all of it. Let yourself receive what's genuinely offered, and every so often, check what you're bringing back into the exchange. Used well, this is a relationship that makes both of you more resourced, not just one of you.

iGenerateOther.text:
In the Five Element cycle, {{my}} generates {{other}} — your energy is the one doing the work here, feeding theirs more often than the reverse. That tends to bring out a genuinely generous version of you: you notice what they need before they ask, you're the one initiating, and it doesn't usually feel like a chore because giving is simply what this energy does. Small doses of this are one of the more rewarding shapes a relationship can take.

What's worth tracking is whether the giving stays sustainable — a generating relationship can quietly tip one-sided if it's never checked, not because anyone's being unfair, but because the flow naturally runs one direction unless you both pay attention to it. Say what you actually need occasionally, not just what you're offering. When it's balanced, this is exactly the kind of relationship where your care visibly makes things better.

otherOvercomesMe.text:
In the Five Element cycle, {{other}} overcomes {{my}} — that's the real source of the tension you're probably picking up on, and it's not a warning sign so much as an honest one. Overcoming relationships tend to push rather than soothe, which is exactly why they stay memorable: something about this connection asks more of you than the easy ones do, and that's often where the real growth happens.

The upside is that friction handled with a little patience tends to teach you more about yourself than a comfortable match ever would — you find out what you're actually capable of when things don't go smoothly. The part that takes real effort is not letting that friction curdle into actual conflict, so it's worth going in with open eyes rather than just curiosity. Communicate a beat more than feels natural here, and this pairing has more to offer than its first impression suggests.

iOvercomeOther.text:
In the Five Element cycle, {{my}} overcomes {{other}} — which puts you in the steadier, more grounding role in this pairing, whether or not either of you has ever put a name to it. People in this position often become the one who keeps things from spiraling, the calm presence in the room even when nobody explicitly asked for it. It's a genuinely useful instinct, and one worth being proud of rather than downplaying.

The thing to watch is the line between grounding and taking over — from the inside, both can feel identical, so it's worth deliberately checking in rather than just assuming your read is the right one. Loosen your grip in at least one place, even when everything in you wants to manage the details. Used with a light hand, this steadiness is exactly what makes the relationship work — not because you're in charge, but because you're dependable.

guide.title: How Ohaeng Works
guide.subtitle: A quick primer if saju is new to you — no prior knowledge required.
guide.sajuHeading: Saju vs. horoscope: what's the difference?
guide.sajuBody1: Western astrology reads the sky — where the sun, moon, and planets sat the moment you were born. Saju (사주, "four pillars") reads the calendar instead. Your birth year, month, day, and hour each get translated into a code from an ancient Chinese and Korean dating system — one built from ten "Heavenly Stems" and twelve "Earthly Branches" cycling together, the same system that names lunar years after animals like the Tiger or the Dragon.
guide.sajuBody2: Stack all four — year, month, day, hour — and you get your "eight characters" (팔자), the full saju chart. It's not more or less legitimate than a sun sign; it's just a different, much older tradition that hasn't had its Co-Star moment in the West yet. Ohaeng is our attempt at that.
guide.elementsBody: Every character in your chart maps to one of five elements — Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal, Water — and whichever shows up most is your dominant element. The elements aren't just labels; they interact. Each one generates the next (Wood feeds Fire, Fire leaves behind Earth, Earth yields Metal, Metal collects Water, Water nourishes Wood) and overcomes another (Wood parts Earth, Earth dams Water, Water douses Fire, Fire melts Metal, Metal chops Wood). That generating-and-overcoming cycle is the actual engine behind your daily fortune and your idol compatibility results — not a coin flip.
guide.accuracyHeading: This isn't a random number generator
guide.accuracyBody: A lot of horoscope-style apps quietly pick a result at random and dress it up as personal. Ohaeng doesn't — it runs your birthdate through lunar-javascript, an open-source calendar engine built on real historical solar-term and sexagenary-cycle data, the same math traditional manseryeok almanacs use. Two people with the same birthday will always get the same chart, and today's fortune is always the actual Five Element relationship between your chart and today's, not noise.
guide.scoreBody: Every score you see — in Compatibility, Idol Match, Drama Match, or Group Match — comes from the same Five Element relationship described above, turned into a number. Same-element pairs start in the low-to-mid 90s, generating relationships (someone feeding your energy, or you feeding theirs) land in the 70s-80s, and overcoming relationships — the tense, push-and-pull kind — sit lower, in the 40s-60s. Every pair also gets a small individual nudge so two pairings with the same relationship type don't come out looking identical. It's not a random roll layered on top of astrology — it's the same math, just expressed as a percentage.
guide.strengthBody: Your Day Master is the Heavenly Stem of your Day Pillar — the character that represents "you" specifically, separate from your overall dominant element. Ohaeng checks how much support that character gets from the rest of your chart: if at least half the other characters share or generate its element, you're a "strong" Day Master; otherwise, you're "weak." Strong doesn't mean better and weak doesn't mean worse — it's a read on whether your core traits show up consistently everywhere you go (strong) or shift more with who's around you (weak). You'll see this reflected on every avatar in the app too: a solid ring means a strong Day Master, a dashed ring means a weak one.
guide.featuresBody: Idol Match and Drama Match both work the same way: enter your birthday and gender, and Ohaeng scans the full roster — every idol group, or all 100 K-drama actors — filtered to the opposite gender, and surfaces whoever scores highest against your chart. Group Match works a little differently: pick one group, and instead of a single best match, you get every member ranked by score, so you can see exactly where your bias lands next to the rest of the lineup.
guide.dataHeading: How We Manage Idol & Actor Data
guide.dataBody1: Right now, Ohaeng's database covers {{groups}} K-pop groups ({{members}} members) and {{actors}} K-drama actors — every birthdate you see in Idol Match, K-Drama Match, and group chemistry mode comes from that pool.
guide.dataBody2: Birthdates are sourced from public fan wikis and reference sites (KProfiles, NamuWiki, Generasia, and similar), cross-checked across at least two independent sources before being added. If a birthdate only shows up on a single low-reliability source, we don't add it — better to leave someone out than get their chart wrong.
guide.dataBody3: We're adding new groups and actors on an ongoing basis. Don't see who you're looking for? There's a request link right on the Idol Match and K-Drama Match pages, or you can reach out through Contact.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.subtitle: Last updated: August 18, 2026
privacy.birthDataBody: Ohaeng is a static site with no backend database. When you enter your birthday — and optionally your name or gender — to get a reading, that information is used entirely inside your own browser to calculate your saju chart. It's never uploaded to or stored on any server we control.
privacy.partnerDataBody: The same applies to the other person's name and birthday you enter for a Compatibility or Romance reading — it's processed in your browser to work out your compatibility and is never stored on a server.
privacy.shareImageBody: When you share a result link, we generate a preview image — showing things like a name and a compatibility score, but never a raw birthdate — so the link looks right when pasted into apps like KakaoTalk or Discord. These images are generated on the fly from the link itself and may be cached on Cloudflare's edge network so repeat views load quickly.
privacy.analyticsBody: We use PostHog to collect anonymous usage analytics — which pages get visited, which buttons get clicked, and similar patterns — so we can understand how people use Ohaeng and improve it. This data isn't linked to your birthday, name, or the contents of any reading you enter.
privacy.storageBody: Ohaeng doesn't use tracking cookies. We use your browser's local storage only to remember your theme (light/dark) and language preference, and — if you've filled out your own birthday once — to pre-fill it for you the next time you open a reading, so you don't have to type it in again. All of this stays on your device and is never sent to a server.
privacy.contactBody: If you have any questions about this policy, reach out through our Contact page.
